title: Moussaka
subtitle: Layered aubergine and lamb mince with bechamel topping
excerpt: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of spiced lamb mince, sliced aubergine, and a thick bechamel sauce. The layers are built up in the tin and baked until golden. It takes patience but most of the time is hands-off in the oven.
sourceNotes: Moussaka is eaten across Greece, the Balkans, and the Middle East in different versions. The Greek version with a bechamel topping was popularised by the Greek chef Nikolaos Tselementes in the early twentieth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool fully, cut into portions, and freeze for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and reheat in the oven at 180C for 25 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the full dish up to 24 hours ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Add 10 minutes to the baking time from cold.

content.text: Rest the moussaka for at least 15 minutes after baking. If you cut it too soon the layers will slide. The rest also lets the bechamel set so each portion holds its shape.
Heat the oven to 190C. Lay the aubergine slices on baking trays. Brush both sides with olive oil and season. Roast for 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender. Set aside.
Brown the lamb mince in a dry large saucepan over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it up. Drain off excess fat if needed.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cinnamon, and allspice and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree, tinned tomatoes, and red wine vinegar. Simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Season well.

Make the bechamel: melt the butter in a saucepan. Add the flour and stir for 1 minute. Add the warm milk gradually, whisking constantly, until smooth and thick. Stir in the nutmeg, half the parmesan, and season. Cool slightly, then beat in the eggs.
Layer in a roasting tin: half the aubergine, all the meat sauce, then the rest of the aubergine. Pour the bechamel over the top. Scatter with remaining parmesan.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and the dish is bubbling at the edges.
Rest for 15 minutes before slicing. Serve with a green salad.

items.cause: Milk was added too fast or was cold.
items.fix: Use warm milk; add slowly while whisking without stopping.

items.cause: Not rested long enough before cutting.
items.fix: Rest at least 15 minutes so layers can set firm.
